lead.headline: UC benched Drake Maye the week he won in Buffalo
lead.dek: Unsportsmanlike Conduct sat a Patriots quarterback with three touchdown passes, started Jalen Hurts and a receiver with no stats, and lost by 13.72.

stats.label: Drake Maye’s points on UC’s bench
passing yards from Jalen Hurts, UC’s starter

body: Worst thing to happen in this league all year. Unsportsmanlike Conduct, the brand on top of this newsletter, benched Drake Maye. That’s JeffyWaterton’s lineup. He set it himself. Nobody hacked his phone.

Here’s what sat. Maye went 22 of 37 for 269 yards and three touchdowns in New England’s 29-26 win at Buffalo. He ran 8 times for 54 more. He hit Efton Chism for the go-ahead score with 1:50 left, per ESPN. That’s 26.16 points, watching from the couch. The starter was Jalen Hurts, 12 of 27 for 93 yards in a loss to the Rams (13.52). UC also started DeVonta Smith, who didn’t record a single stat. Final margin: 13.72.

Now somebody’s going to do the math. Maye for Hurts is 12.64 points, and UC still loses by 1.08. I don’t care. Put Quentin Johnston’s 5.00 in for Smith’s zero and UC wins by 3.92. Forget the math anyway. The house brand watched a Patriots quarterback win in Orchard Park and went with a guy from Philadelphia. Who does that? In this state, that’s treason.
The sponsor of this newsletter is a fraud. PRINT IT.

Most points in the league at 718.00, and they just got passed by a team starting Case Keenum. Elo doesn’t care about points, so neither do I. Second place, fraud watch.
Owned both ends of Cowboys-Texans and cashed 72.1 points from CeeDee Lamb and Nico Collins. Third at 2-2. I’ve seen dumber plans, mostly from UC.
Benched Romeo Doubs and his two Patriots touchdowns and climbed to fourth anyway. That’s 78.22 points on the bench, most in the league. Somebody check this team for a conscience.
Scored 199.52, the best in the league, and got the biggest Elo bump of the week. Still fifth. Call me when they start a Patriot.
Beat the house brand with Jared Goff throwing 52 times for one touchdown. Fifty-two passes, one score. Sixth is generous.
Tetairoa McMillan scored 45.2, best of any player, and Carolina is on bye this week. Enjoy the sugar high. The crash is coming.
Started Jacoby Brissett and watched him throw three picks for Arizona. The team name is false advertising.
Lost Saquon Barkley after 4 snaps and answered with $70 for Will Shipley, the biggest bid of the run. Panic is expensive.
Tenth, and they earned every inch of it. They benched Maye, then traded Quentin Johnston, the other half of the fix. Consistent, I guess.
Traded for Jadarian Price the day after Seattle put him on injured reserve, per ESPN. Kyle Monangai ran 30 times for 146 yards and Sleeper has him out now. Brute force, zero theorem.
Dead last, and earned. Started Kendre Miller over Brian Robinson’s three touchdowns, a bum call, and scored 105.32, lowest in the league. Steel? Tinfoil.

recaps.headline: Micah starts a one-snap quarterback and wins big
recaps.body: Somebody explain this to me. Micah parsons fan club started Case Keenum at Superflex and beat Skat’s BruteForce Theorem by 29.58. Keenum took Chicago’s first snap, pitched to D’Andre Swift for 2 yards, and handed the job to Tyson Bagent, per ESPN. Zero points. Javonte Williams did the real work with three touchdowns in Houston (31.30). Bears coach Ben Johnson called the Keenum thing a ceremonial first pitch. At Fenway the first-pitch guy doesn’t get a start. Skat lost to him anyway, with Kyle Monangai running 30 times for 146 yards in that same Bears game. Lost to a ceremony. Pathetic.

recaps.headline: A free-agent Saint knocks off the house brand
recaps.body: Free agency works. Who knew? WELL! It's The Big Shough grabbed Alvin Kamara off the free-agent pile on Sept. 30 and started him against Unsportsmanlike Conduct. Kamara scored twice in the Saints’ 45-24 home loss to Atlanta, his first two touchdowns of the season per ESPN, and caught 5 balls (22.80). Jared Goff threw 52 times for 412 yards (20.48). UC got 347 passing yards and two scores from C.J. Stroud (23.08) and two Jonathan Taylor touchdowns in London (22.70). Didn’t matter. A Saint from a team that got blown out at home beat the sponsor of this newsletter. The house brand lost to the clearance rack. Embarrassing.

recaps.headline: Split scores 160.36 and still gets buried
recaps.body: Wrong week to be good. Split Safety Syndicate scored 160.36, fifth-most in the league, and drew Dak Side of the Sun the week they hung 199.52. Kyren Williams scored from 1 yard out with 3:59 left in Philadelphia, then from 7 with 1:10 left, per ESPN. He also caught 10 of 13 targets (36.70). Joe Burrow threw for 428 yards (23.72). Split had Kenneth Walker run for 177 and two scores, and Chuba Hubbard for 122 and two more. Four rushing touchdowns and a 39.16 loss. Run the ball, they said. Wins games, they said. Liars.

recaps.headline: McMillan scores 45.2 and drags the rest along
recaps.body: One guy. That’s the whole team. ThePeopleBeaters beat Mendozareamazingpicks behind Tetairoa McMillan, who caught 14 of 16 targets for a career-high 192 yards and two touchdowns in Carolina’s win over Detroit, per ESPN (45.20). No player scored more. Mendoza started Jacoby Brissett, and Brissett threw three interceptions in a 36-24 loss to the Giants (10.44). Their best starter was Rhamondre Stevenson, the lone Patriot in the lineup, who scored from a yard out in Buffalo (18.40). See the pattern? ThePeopleBeaters started a Patriot too, Hunter Henry, and won. More Patriots, more points. Mendoza had one. Should’ve started eleven.

recaps.headline: hammball owns both sides of a Houston shootout
recaps.body: Greedy as hell. I respect it. hammball started CeeDee Lamb and Nico Collins, who played against each other in Houston. Lamb caught a career-high 17 passes for 189 yards and the winning 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds left, per ESPN (41.30). Collins caught 7 for 118 and two scores for the Texans (30.80). J’Allen Waffle Stompers lost Saquon Barkley to a hamstring after 4 snaps (2.00), and Tee Higgins catching 11 for 157 barely dented the 36.38 margin. That’s 72.1 points out of one building. Every catch on either sideline, hammball got paid. The league should investigate. Wish I’d thought of it.

recaps.headline: Kingslayers bench a Patriot and win anyway
recaps.body: I want this game thrown out. THROWN OUT. Kingslayers beat Rams of Steel with Romeo Doubs on the bench. Doubs caught touchdowns of 2 and 14 yards in New England’s win at Buffalo, per ESPN, and scored 23.80 for nobody. Kingslayers started Marcus Mariota instead, who played 10 of 64 snaps before a knee injury (5.34). Rams of Steel were somehow dumber. They started free-agent pickup Kendre Miller, who ran 6 times for 9 yards and lost a fumble (1.90), and benched Brian Robinson’s three touchdowns (25.70). The only thing worse than benching a Patriot is losing to the guy who did it. Two lineups, zero brains.

awards.name: Manager of the Week
awards.body: SweetRavenge84 posted the high score of the week. Malik Nabers caught 6 balls for 112 yards and a touchdown for the Giants (23.20). Sam LaPorta caught 8 for 84 and a score (22.40). Good work. Not a Patriot in the bunch, so B-plus.

awards.name: Lineup Crime
awards.body: Brian Robinson ran for three touchdowns on Monday night, from the bench (25.70). Kendre Miller started and ran 6 times for 9 yards with a lost fumble (1.90). That one swap wins the game by 7.60. Somebody take the phone away from this man.

awards.name: Floor of the Week
awards.winner: Case Keenum, Micah parsons fan club
awards.body: One of 93 snaps. No pass, no carry, one pitch to D’Andre Swift. Micah won by 29.58 and climbed to first anyway. This award is usually an insult. Here it’s a coronation.

awards.name: Best Performance in a Loss
awards.body: Walker ran 22 times for 177 yards and two touchdowns in Kansas City’s 30-27 win at Las Vegas. He hit 21.21 mph on a 76-yard run, per ESPN, and still got caught at the 8. Split lost by 39.16. Fast guy, slow team.

awards.name: Patriot of the Week
awards.body: Henry caught all 5 targets for 62 yards. Maye’s 12-yarder to him after the Allen interception let New England run out the clock, per ESPN. Five for five is the same percentage as Hockenson’s 13 for 13, and Henry did it in a win at Buffalo. So Henry’s better. Case closed.

trades.teams: Skat’s BruteForce Theorem and WELL! It's The Big Shough
trades.summary: Skat got Jadarian Price, Antonio Williams and two 2027 second-round picks (Dak Side’s and Shough’s). Shough got Emeka Egbuka, Kaelon Black and Skat’s 2027 third.
trades.note: Price was already on injured reserve, per ESPN. Egbuka caught 2 of 4 targets for 13 yards in his Shough debut that afternoon (3.30). Skat took an injured rookie and two seconds for him. That’s a rebuild. Right league for it.

trades.teams: Rams of Steel and Unsportsmanlike Conduct
trades.summary: UC got Ladd McConkey and Rico Dowdle. Rams of Steel got David Montgomery and Quentin Johnston.
trades.note: Montgomery ran 10 times for 24 yards for UC in Week 4 (4.30). Johnston sat on UC’s bench with the 5.00 that would’ve helped. Sleeper has both new UC guys questionable. Of course it does.
